title: scope.md frontmatter
description: Schema for the frontmatter of scope.md, the canonical gating artifact for the define phase. Validated by the gate engine before define can be marked complete.

id.description: Ticket id this scope traces back to — must match the id on the intent.md it was drafted from

business_case.description: Why this is worth doing — the value/ROI case. Pulled from the source PRD/RFC when one is linked (intent.md's source_docs), not invented.

out_of_scope.description: Explicitly excluded, not just unmentioned — this is what keeps define's scope from silently ballooning back into what plan already rejected

success_metrics.description: Measurable definitions of success — checked against production outcomes after launch, via this client's own observability tooling rather than a dedicated measure phase in this PDLC

dependencies.description: Other systems, teams, or tickets this scope depends on

impact_assessment.description: Who/what is affected — blast radius across systems, teams, customers

concept_prototyping.description: Summary of any concept prototyping / value testing already done (by the client's own product process) — link out rather than re-describe if it lives elsewhere. Leave empty, don't fabricate, when none was done for a change this small.

event_storming.description: Summary or link to event-storming output (domain events/commands/aggregates) when the change is complex enough to warrant it. Leave empty for straightforward changes — not every ticket needs domain modeling.

feature_prioritization.description: MoSCoW-style breakdown — mainly relevant when an epic covers multiple features/stories being prioritized against each other

open_questions.description: Anything this schema wants that the source intent.md / linked PRD-RFC didn't have. Must be empty, or explicitly waived, before design can close.

source_docs.description: Carried forward from intent.md — the PRD/RFC this scope was actually derived from, if any

approved_by.description: Required when status is approved — must be the product owner (phase-graph.yaml's approval role for define), and distinct from the author when enforce_segregation_of_duties is on

approval_evidence.description: Required when status is approved (require_approval_evidence in phase-graph.yaml) — a link to the Jira comment/Slack message/email where the product owner actually approved this, since they typically have no git/GitHub/Cursor/Claude access to approve it there directly.

approvals.description: One entry per approving role. Only needed when this artifact's gate asks for more than one signature (a quorum or tier strategy in .pdlc/phase-graph.yaml). A single-approver gate keeps using status/approved_by/approval_evidence. Every entry needs its own evidence link when require_approval_evidence is on — one link does not cover two people.

role.description: The approval role named by this gate in .pdlc/phase-graph.yaml, e.g. product_owner. An entry for a role the gate did not ask for does not count toward it.

by.description: The person who decided. Required when status is approved.

evidence.description: Link to where this person actually approved or declined — the Jira comment, Slack message or change record.
